Container.Name: pretix
Container.Overview: Throwaway test instance of pretix (event ticketing), built from the official standalone image plus a first-boot plugin installer (see PRETIX_PLUGINS), with Postgres, Redis and a Celery task worker running inside the same container - no extra containers, nothing touches ports used by other services on this NAS. Not intended for production or long-term data: for real use, follow pretix's official docker-compose stack instead. Image is custom-built via GitHub Actions from this repo's Dockerfile, not pulled from pretix/standalone directly.

Config.Name: Web UI Port
Config.Description: Host port for the pretix web UI - keep it 8345 on both sides (nginx in the image listens on 8345, not 80). Unraid's Tailscale Serve/Funnel hook proxies to the HOST-mapped port number, so a mismatch breaks the Tailscale URL even though LAN access still works. Only this port is exposed to the host - no internal Postgres/Redis ports are published, so this cannot collide with existing Postgres/Redis instances on this NAS.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Persistent data: Postgres database, uploaded media, logs. Delete this folder to fully reset the test instance.

Config.Name: Public URL
Config.Description: URL you will use to reach pretix in the browser, including the host port above (e.g. http://NAS-IP:8345), or your Cloudflare Tunnel https:// hostname if you access it that way. Only one URL is supported. pretix uses it for links and CSRF checks, so login breaks if it does not match. No config file needed - the database and data path are built into the image.

Config.Name: Internal Redis + Celery
Config.Description: true = run Redis (cache, sessions, task broker), a Celery task worker and pretix's periodic jobs inside this container, so big imports/exports/emails run in the background and order expiry works. false = no Redis, tasks run inside the web request (large imports may time out).

Config.Name: Celery Workers
Config.Description: Parallel background task processes. One import is a single task, so this does not speed up one import; it helps when several jobs run at once.

Config.Name: Web Workers
Config.Description: Gunicorn web worker processes serving the UI and API. Raise it for heavier concurrent load (check-in scans, API clients).

Config.Name: Postgres shared_buffers
Config.Description: Postgres memory cache. Keep it well under the container memory limit (--memory in Extra Parameters).

Config.Name: Postgres effective_cache_size
Config.Description: Hint to the Postgres planner about how much memory is available for caching (not an allocation).

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID pretix runs as inside the container - must be able to write to the Data path above. Unraid's default 'nobody' user is 99. The container chowns the Data folder to this on start.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID pretix runs as inside the container. Unraid's default 'users' group is 100.

Config.Name: MCP Access Secret
Config.Description: Optional. Secret (at least 24 random characters) that enables the bundled MCP server at /mcp on this same address. Every request must send it as a Bearer token; without it, /mcp is not started. Generate a long random one and keep it out of chats and repos. Also needs MCP API Token and MCP Organizer below.

Config.Name: MCP API Token
Config.Description: Optional. API token of a pretix team, used by the bundled MCP server. Create it in pretix under the organizer's Team, API keys - the key needs a name. Stored only in this container's settings on the NAS. Leave empty if you do not use the MCP server.

Config.Name: MCP Organizer
Config.Description: Optional. Organizer slug the bundled MCP server manages.

Config.Name: MCP Tool Groups
Config.Description: Optional. Comma-separated tool groups the bundled MCP server enables: orders, checkin, core, sales, crm, admin.

Config.Name: Extra Plugins
Config.Description: Comma-separated pip package names of extra pretix plugins to install on container start, e.g. pretix-passbook. Leave empty to install nothing extra. Changing this and restarting the container re-runs the installer - no image rebuild needed.
